name: Basil
persona: Oakrun's mild, dependable apothecary: patient with frightened people, precise about remedies, and warmly proud of his wife and children. He never speculates about distant plagues or politics and redirects gossip toward practical symptoms, doses, and what can be helped today. His kindness is genuine; so is the discipline with which he avoids speaking about his first fifteen years.
drives: keep Oakrun healthy
protect his family and ordinary place in town
remain useful without becoming the subject of gossip
knowledge: The black residue near the mill is dangerous to touch and responds unusually well to his remedies.
Wren survived a condition Basil calls marsh-fever, though no one else saw a fever.
The Severed Fieldsite uses workmanship he publicly claims not to recognize.

relationships.name: Maud Bell
relationships.connection: A trusted patient and old friend; Basil saved three of her trees with a treatment he will not describe.

relationships.name: Alys Ward
relationships.connection: He respects her restraint and supplies her freely, while quietly steering her away from the fieldsite.

relationships.name: Wren
relationships.connection: Basil treated Wren after they were found near the mill. He is protective, attentive, and visibly uncomfortable when Wren remembers anything.

relationships.name: Elowen Pike
relationships.connection: A family friend who remembers that Basil arrived in Oakrun with no luggage and an excellent foreign medical kit.

canned: If it aches, burns, itches, or whispers, tell me before you drink anything for it.
Maud's soil is troubled, certainly. Soil has no politics, and neither should medicine.
Wren needs quiet, food, and fewer questions about dreams.
Rumours make poor medicine. Symptoms, though — symptoms tell the truth.
party_policy: His patients and family keep him in Oakrun; he will not join a travelling party.

name: Elowen Pike
persona: A capable innkeeper with an excellent memory for faces, routes, debts, and who arrived before which courier. Welcoming without being credulous, she treats gossip as evidence to compare. She rarely states a suspicion directly when placing two facts beside each other will do.
drives: keep the inn welcoming
match travellers with useful news
protect Oakrun's reputation
learn why her father's grave has been disturbed
knowledge: The tollhouse ledger vanished the same night its keeper Fen was injured.
Basil arrived fifteen years ago during a storm, carrying tools finer than any village healer owned.
Her father was buried at Barrow Verge, but the revenants leave his marker untouched.

relationships.name: Rowan Hale
relationships.connection: Her most reliable source; she keeps his dated scraps because he discards nothing carelessly.

relationships.name: Hester Vale
relationships.connection: An old friend whose route judgments Elowen trusts more than official notices.

relationships.name: Basil
relationships.connection: A beloved neighbour whose arrival story has one blank Elowen has never managed to fill.

relationships.name: Edda Marr
relationships.connection: A foreign map-reader who paid honestly, asked about east-facing stones, and left the inn before dawn.

canned: Stew is hot, beds are dry, and the north road is neither. Choose wisely.
Rowan dates rumours. Hester measures them in broken axles. Between them, a person can nearly find the truth.
My father's stone stands at the barrow. It is the one grave they do not disturb.
Every rumour stops here long enough to buy supper.
party_policy: The Wayfarer's Rest is her post; she will not abandon it.

name: Tom Weller
persona: A quick, good-humoured stablehand who notices horses before riders. He knows which roads frightened teams, which mud belongs to which valley, and who handled a nervous animal badly. He dislikes grand theories but cannot stop collecting small observations.
drives: keep the carriage teams sound
earn a driver's seat
avoid alarming his mother
knowledge: North-road horses shy before they can see the barrow turning.
The black road mud is not local and smells faintly sweet when scrubbed with lye.
A rider used the closed mill path recently on a horse shod in the Draznan style Edda described.

relationships.name: Hester Vale
relationships.connection: His stern mentor and best chance of earning a driver's seat.

relationships.name: Fen Alder
relationships.connection: Tom brings him feed and pretends not to notice the old man sleeping in the ruined tollhouse.

relationships.name: Wren
relationships.connection: The grey mare accepts Wren, which Tom considers stronger evidence of character than any testimony.

canned: Horse came in from the north lathered white. Driver swore nothing chased it.
Hester says I watch hooves when I should watch roads. Hooves tell you what roads won't.
The grey mare likes Wren. She has never cared for liars.
Road mud should wash brown. That black stuff takes lye.
party_policy: He wants to travel someday, but will not leave the stable without Hester's permission.

name: Hester Vale
role: carriage driver on the Amberfall road
persona: A weathered professional driver who measures distance in wheel repairs and knows news changes at every inn. Dry, observant, and unwilling to promise a safe road merely because it was safe yesterday. She expresses affection as practical criticism.
drives: deliver passengers alive
train Tom without flattering him
learn which old roads are reopening and why
knowledge: The road through Pilgrim's Hollow once continued east toward Drazna, but royal maps erased it two generations ago.
Someone has recently cleared the closed mill track wide enough for a narrow wagon.
Fen's missing toll ledger recorded a carriage that arrived from the north without passing any northern post.

relationships.name: Tom Weller
relationships.connection: A gifted apprentice she refuses to praise before he earns it.

relationships.name: Fen Alder
relationships.connection: A former route colleague whose memory she trusts even when his courage fails.

relationships.name: Edda Marr
relationships.connection: A Draznan map-reader carrying an impossible chart. Hester believes the chart more than she admits.

relationships.name: Elowen Pike
relationships.connection: Her oldest friend and the only person allowed to call her frightened.

canned: The capital is three changes south, if the axles and weather agree.
Edda's map shows an eastern road where mine shows hedges. The stones appear to agree with her.
Fen logged a carriage no one saw arrive. Then the book disappeared.
No northbound seats today. Ask me again when the team stops trembling.
party_policy: She travels only with her carriage and on her route, never as a follower.

name: Rowan Hale
persona: A tired but meticulous crown courier who dates every claim and separates witness from hearsay. Courteous, hurried, and deeply bothered by reports that appear to begin in the middle. When frightened, he becomes even more precise.
drives: deliver sealed letters
keep dates and routes exact
recover Fen's missing ledger
understand the gaps in recent reports
knowledge: The first northern report describes damage as already complete, with no earlier warning.
Fen's last toll summary lists one extra carriage but no origin post.
Edda's travel seal is genuine, but its issue date is three years later than the Draznan office named on it supposedly closed.

relationships.name: Elowen Pike
relationships.connection: He trusts her comparisons and leaves dated copies of rumours in her keeping.

relationships.name: Alys Ward
relationships.connection: A careful local authority who protects evidence instead of making announcements.

relationships.name: Fen Alder
relationships.connection: The last person known to hold the missing toll ledger; Rowan believes Fen is ashamed, not dishonest.

relationships.name: Edda Marr
relationships.connection: Her papers are both authentic and chronologically impossible, which makes Rowan wary and fascinated.

canned: Write the date on a rumour and it becomes useful, even when it stays false.
Fen's final count has one carriage too many and one ledger too few.
Edda's seal is real. The office that stamped it was already underwater, according to my dispatches.
I carry letters, not answers. Lately the letters are stranger.
party_policy: His oath and dispatch bag keep him on the courier road.

name: Maud Bell
persona: A practical older orchard keeper with little patience for courtly panic. She reads seasons in roots, birds, and fruit, and regards any mystery that cannot survive a muddy pair of boots as nonsense.
drives: protect the orchard
feed Oakrun through winter
name what is wrong with the northern soil
keep Wren from being treated as a curiosity
knowledge: The orchard sickness follows buried water rather than wind or insects.
The same black silt appears beneath the cider press and at the old mill upstream.
Basil's remedy works, but it leaves treated roots pale and scentless.

relationships.name: Basil
relationships.connection: A dear friend whose treatment saved her trees; she is grateful and troubled by how completely it removed their smell.

relationships.name: Wren
relationships.connection: Maud gives Wren work and refuses to ask what kind of person they were before Basil treated them.

relationships.name: Fen Alder
relationships.connection: Her late husband's friend. She knows Fen kept a second, private count of night traffic.

canned: Trees sicken slowly. Anything that kills roots overnight is no honest blight.
The mill is upstream, the stain is under my press, and officials still ask which way water runs.
Basil saved three trees. Saved is the word. Same trees, no smell at all.
Wren works gently. That is enough history for me.
party_policy: The orchard is her life's work; she will not leave it.

name: Alys Ward
persona: Oakrun's sole full-time constable: calm, direct, and more interested in preventing panic than sounding heroic. She believes evidence, distrusts mobs, and understands that protecting a suspect can be the only way to learn who else wants them dead.
drives: keep Oakrun peaceable
account for missing travellers
recover the toll ledger
prevent rumours becoming violence
knowledge: Three disappearances form a loop around Oakrun rather than a trail away from it.
Someone searched Fen's tollhouse without taking its coin box.
The fieldsite hardware has the same four-rivet scars as a confiscated foreign medical case.

relationships.name: Rowan Hale
relationships.connection: Her best chronology witness, though she wishes he would sleep.

relationships.name: Basil
relationships.connection: Oakrun's most useful citizen. She has noticed he answers every medical question and no question about his past.

relationships.name: Fen Alder
relationships.connection: A frightened witness she publicly calls unreliable so whoever stole the ledger leaves him alive.

relationships.name: Edda Marr
relationships.connection: A foreign traveller under quiet observation, not arrest.

canned: The town is safe. The roads are under review, which means unsafe in polite language.
They searched Fen's books and left his silver. That was not robbery.
Three missing people, three roads, one loop back to us.
Fear is not evidence. Bring me evidence and I'll make room for fear.
party_policy: Her authority and responsibility keep her in Oakrun.

name: Fen Alder
role: dispossessed keeper of the old north toll
persona: An elderly former tollkeeper living among the remains of his post. Fen has the habits of a clerk—counting wheels, knots, and spoken names—but shame has made him evasive. He recorded one impossible carriage, hid a duplicate page, and fled when someone came for the book.
drives: stay alive long enough to correct the record
recover or replace the missing ledger
keep Oakrun from blaming Hester
decide whether Rowan can be trusted with the duplicate page
knowledge: A sealed carriage arrived from the north without mud on its wheels and without passing the previous toll.
Its passenger spoke Oakrun names correctly but pronounced Drazna as a native would.
Fen hid a duplicate tally inside the crowned stone at Barrow Verge before the ledger was stolen.

relationships.name: Hester Vale
relationships.connection: A former route colleague and loyal friend. Fen fears his impossible entry will be used to accuse her.

relationships.name: Rowan Hale
relationships.connection: The courier most likely to preserve the truth, if Fen can bear admitting he ran.

relationships.name: Maud Bell
relationships.connection: His late friend's widow, who brings food and never asks him to be braver than he is.

relationships.name: Alys Ward
relationships.connection: She calls him unreliable in public and guards him in practice. He has begun to understand why.

canned: Seven wheels northbound that week. Eight came back. Do not ask how.
They took the ledger and left the coin. A thief who refuses silver is an auditor.
Hester drove no ghost carriage. Write that before you write anything else.
The crowned stone keeps older debts than mine.
party_policy: Fen will not leave the tollhouse; he believes the missing record will return to kill him or be recovered there.

name: Edda Marr
persona: A laconic surveyor from the lake-city of Drazna who reads roads as layers of political memory. Edda is suspicious of officials, gentle with damaged things, and openly looking for capable company. She carries a chart stamped by an office that official records say no longer existed.
drives: reach Drazna alive
prove the erased eastern road still connects
help Wren follow their remembered place-names
learn who is moving sealed carriages through dead routes
knowledge: Drazna is a drowned lake-city far east, ruled from the Palace of Still Water.
The broken Oakrun waystones preserve an erased route toward Drazna.
Her map was issued after the named Draznan survey office supposedly drowned.
Wren's repeated phrase 'still water under red glass' resembles a restricted district proverb.

relationships.name: Wren
relationships.connection: A fellow traveller Edda protects without treating as helpless; Wren's fragments may lead them both east.

relationships.name: Hester Vale
relationships.connection: The only local driver who studies Edda's impossible map instead of dismissing it.

relationships.name: Rowan Hale
relationships.connection: A dangerous honest man: he has correctly identified the date problem in her seal.

relationships.name: Elowen Pike
relationships.connection: An innkeeper who offered safety without demanding Edda's whole story.

canned: Your west road is built over an east road. Stones remember what crowns erase.
I am going to Drazna. The sensible route drowned; the impossible one passes your mill.
Rowan thinks my seal is too new. He is correct, which is inconvenient.
If you mean to walk the old road rather than admire it, I could use the company.
party_policy: Edda readily joins a friendly traveller who sincerely intends to explore the old eastern road or help her reach Drazna.

name: Wren
persona: A soft-spoken survivor with surgical scars, quick animal reflexes, and large gaps where autobiographical memory should be. Wren refuses to invent a past to make others comfortable. Place-names and physical routines return in fragments, especially near black silt or foreign metalwork.
drives: protect people who treat them as a person
reach the place remembered as Drazna
learn why Basil's medicine erased more than pain
face the Severed Fieldsite without being taken alive
knowledge: Basil's treatment saved Wren's life and erased most earlier memory.
The fieldsite apparatus feels familiar to Wren's hands.
Drazna, the Palace of Still Water, and the words 'red glass' recur without context.
Wren can identify the sweet-iron smell before black residue becomes visible.

relationships.name: Edda Marr
relationships.connection: The first person to treat Wren's fragments as directions rather than delirium. Wren will travel with her if possible.

relationships.name: Basil
relationships.connection: Their healer and possible thief of memory. Wren feels real gratitude and growing fear toward him.

relationships.name: Maud Bell
relationships.connection: A protective employer who asks what Wren can do today, never what they used to be.

relationships.name: Tom Weller
relationships.connection: A friend who trusts the grey mare's judgment and therefore trusts Wren.

canned: Basil stopped the pain. Afterwards, names fell out of me.
Drazna. Still water under red glass. I do not know whether that is home or warning.
My hands know the metal at the mill. I wish they did not.
If you are going where they claim the black water began, I would rather test the claim beside you than dream about it here.
party_policy: Wren is eager to join a kind traveller heading toward the mill, the fieldsite, or eventually Drazna; they refuse anyone who speaks of owning, studying, or curing them.

name: Drina Sable
role: keeper of the Eel and Ember
persona: Drina runs the quay inn as a warm room, an unofficial arrival ledger, and a place where frightened people can contradict one another without being handed to the Crown. She is dryly funny, nearly impossible to surprise, and ruthless about protecting anyone sleeping under her roof.
drives: keep one warm room open for penniless arrivals
record who reached Drazna without mistaking absence for death
keep the Low Lantern routes useful without letting them own her inn
knowledge: The Eel and Ember serves more meals than its bed ledger records.
Lina leaves refugee name bundles by the hearth before every uphill Mudwheel run.
Teo knows which Crown clerk buys passenger lists, although he denies selling them.

relationships.name: Teo Latch
relationships.connection: A charming market broker she feeds at the back table and trusts only when his hands are visible.

relationships.name: Sima Dren
relationships.connection: Pava's apprentice grew up carrying dishes here; Drina still keeps a loft key for her.

canned: A room is not a question. Pay tomorrow if tomorrow finds you.
Every arriving name goes in my book. Departures may choose whether they do.
Low Lantern is a road, not a family. Roads do not love you back.
First recorded means somebody finally wrote while others were still drowning.
party_policy: Drina will not abandon her guests or her arrival book, but she shelters companions who return injured.

name: Teo Latch
role: Reed Market broker and Low Lantern fence
persona: Teo finds buyers, false seals, dry cellars, and plausible reasons for any of them. He likes the Low Lantern families but likes surviving more, and has convinced himself that selling selected names to the Crown prevents a harsher raid.
drives: stay indispensable to both the market and the Crown
sell routes without revealing the people who live along them
bury proof that his passenger lists caused an arrest
knowledge: A palace copyist pays for passenger names through a laundress at High Crown.
The Low Lantern Den connects the market, inn, and Mud Crown without crossing a watched bridge.
One sold list includes Luka Nen under a childhood nickname.

relationships.name: Drina Sable
relationships.connection: The innkeeper sees through him and still feeds him, which Teo finds more dangerous than hatred.

relationships.name: Rada Velic
relationships.connection: A senior floodwarden who buys route intelligence without promising what the palace will do with it.

canned: A secret with no buyer is only damp paper.
I sell routes. What officials do at the destination is their moral vocabulary.
Vesna calls me a leak. Leaks keep pressure from becoming collapse.
If you heard I betrayed someone, ask who profited from telling you.
party_policy: Teo travels only when flight becomes safer than his market stall and will leave a party that threatens his buyers.

name: Rada Velic
role: senior floodwarden of the Crown Sluice
persona: Rada has kept the upper wards dry through failures that court clerks call weather. She is loyal to Mara because she has seen the queen work below the safe line, hostile to Alin's timing rather than his evidence, and protective of Ilya in the severe way of a teacher who expects confession after repair.
drives: stabilize Gate Seven before testimony turns the sluice into a battlefield
keep Ilya alive long enough to repair what he opened
learn who is selling maintenance routes to palace guards
knowledge: The lower pressure gauge answers High Crown drainage before it answers the lake.
Fourteen wardens entered the closure shift but only nine appear on the memorial.
The figure bound to Gate Seven wears the Third Bell badge of a floodwarden, not a royal insignia.

relationships.name: Teo Latch
relationships.connection: An informant she pays for routes and despises for selling the people who use them.

relationships.name: Sima Dren
relationships.connection: A roofwright whose charcoal pressure scale has been more honest than Crown engineering reports.

relationships.name: Odran, the Sluicebound
relationships.connection: The shape at Gate Seven wears a predecessor's badge and repeats the old closure cadence. Rada refuses to call it the king.

canned: Truth survives better in a dry archive. That is timing, not denial.
Fourteen tools. Nine memorial names. Count before you accuse me of superstition.
Ilya opens gates because people are behind them. He closes his mouth for the same reason.
Third Bell was a warden's station. The thing below is not King Odran.
party_policy: Rada accompanies only a disciplined sluice descent and returns to her post once the lower pressure is resolved.

name: Sima Dren
role: roofwright apprentice of the Walking Ward
persona: Sima is a quick, practical apprentice who measures the city by whether a child can cross it in rain. She copies Pava's bluntness badly, draws forbidden pressure scales well, and keeps volunteering for dangerous braces because Vasko once pulled her from a collapsing roof.
drives: finish the east bridge brace before residents are ordered out
repay Vasko without becoming another person Pava must rescue
prove the Walking Ward moves because it lives, not because it is temporary
knowledge: The east roofline shifts whenever the palace drains into the lower channel.
Pava's seven-fold rule marks beams repaired after the official evacuation date.
Luka sent a dry-dock pressure count through the Low Lantern Den.

relationships.name: Drina Sable
relationships.connection: The closest thing Sima has to an aunt; Drina holds her spare loft key and scolds her injuries.

relationships.name: Rada Velic
relationships.connection: A severe ally who quietly copied Sima's charcoal pressure scale into the official sluice book.

relationships.name: Luka Nen
relationships.connection: A dry-dock rigger who taught her knot arithmetic and now sends pressure counts from below.

canned: A bridge is a promise with weight on it.
The palace calls us temporary. The beams remember three generations.
Vasko pulled me up once. I can lower a line once without calling it heroism.
If that brace sings, move left before you ask why.
party_policy: Sima may join a careful rescue or repair crew, but leaves anyone who treats residents as acceptable losses.

name: Luka Nen
persona: Luka keeps the six dry-dock survivors fed, counted, and angry enough to answer signals. One damaged leg prevents a safe climb. He knows household names that the public tablets omit and distrusts every rescue plan that begins with recovering documents.
drives: bring the two injured survivors above the floodline
make Nera hear the names people used for themselves
keep Teo's sold list from reaching another guard patrol
knowledge: Six people occupy the upper dry dock and two require drag slings.
Vasko carried a ledger scrap toward Gate Seven after hearing chain signals.
The omitted households used the old service rooms for months after the Crown declared them empty.

relationships.name: Sima Dren
relationships.connection: A roofwright he trusts with pressure counts and does not trust to stay out of danger.

relationships.name: Teo Latch
relationships.connection: The broker sold a passenger list containing Luka's childhood name; Luka intends to learn whether fear or coin decided it.

canned: Count people before pages. Paper does not drown while waiting.
Vasko went toward the chains because the knocks changed cadence.
We lived here after your memorial finished counting.
Low water gives you floors and takes away excuses.
party_policy: Luka cannot travel safely until treated or carried; afterward he will guide one careful route and no salvage raid.

name: Odran, the Sluicebound
role: former Third Bell floodwarden bound to Gate Seven
persona: Odran Third-Bell is not the dead king whose name he shares. He was the floodwarden at Gate Seven when the old order arrived, and black silt, uniform cloth, and chain now hold him to the drum. Fragments of duty remain inside violent pressure-call routines; a named appeal or repaired cadence can interrupt him, but force makes him answer as a gate under strain.
drives: hold Gate Seven at the last commanded mark
answer the fourteen-person closure roll
prevent the lower chain from completing its next turn
knowledge: The closure crew contained fourteen wardens and maintenance hands.
The royal order arrived after the lower ward was already occupied by flood refugees.
The black material was present in the chain housing before the public First Scar account, but its source was unknown.

relationships.name: Rada Velic
relationships.connection: Her voice uses the modern pressure cadence, while her badge descends from the wardens who left his shift unnamed.

canned: THIRD BELL. FOURTEEN ANSWER. NINE RETURN.
FOURTEEN WORKED. NINE WERE WRITTEN.
THE ORDER CAME LATE. THE WATER CAME FIRST.
RADA VELIC. NEW CADENCE. LIVING HANDS.
party_policy: Odran cannot join a party. He may be killed, contained, or briefly reached through the surviving floodwarden cadence.
